name: Airbus C-295 (India build)

what_it_is.prose: The Airbus C-295 is a twin-engine tactical transport aircraft being procured by the Indian Air Force to replace its legacy fleet of Avro HS-748 aircraft. The programme, signed on 24 September 2021 for ₹21,935 crore (~$2.5 billion), comprises 56 aircraft: 16 imported fly-away from Airbus Defence and Space's Seville facility in Spain (deliveries began September 2023), and 40 to be assembled in India by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) at a dedicated Final Assembly Line (FAL) in Vadodara, Gujarat — the first private commercial transport aircraft FAL in India. The first India-built C-295 was rolled out in October 2025. The C-295 has a payload capacity of up to 9 tonnes, a range of up to 2,700 nautical miles (5,000 km) fully loaded, and can carry up to 71 troops, 24 stretchers, or 48 paratroopers. The aircraft is powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127G engines. The programme represents a landmark for Indian aerospace manufacturing — it is the first time a private Indian company (TASL) will assemble a complete military transport aircraft, with progressive indigenisation of airframe components and sub-assemblies. The programme also includes a Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) facility and a Training Centre (with full-flight simulator) at the Vadodara FAL. Cross-link to Military Aerospace vertical — the C-295 is a transport aircraft, not a combat aircraft, but is included in the Defence Atlas due to its strategic airlift role.

deployments_procurement.summary: India signed a ₹21,935 crore contract on 24 September 2021 for 56 C-295 aircraft (16 imported from Spain + 40 built by TASL in India). The first fly-away aircraft was delivered from Airbus Seville in September 2023. The first India-assembled C-295 was rolled out from the Vadodara FAL in October 2025. Deliveries are scheduled to continue through 2031.

faq.question: Why is the C-295 programme significant for Indian aerospace manufacturing?
faq.answer: The C-295 programme represents the first time a private Indian company (Tata Advanced Systems Limited, TASL) will assemble a complete military transport aircraft. The Vadodara Final Assembly Line (FAL) is the first private commercial transport aircraft FAL in India. Of the 56 aircraft, 16 are imported fly-away from Airbus Seville (Spain) and 40 are assembled in India by TASL, with progressive indigenisation of airframe components and sub-assemblies. The programme also includes an MRO facility and a Training Centre with full-flight simulator at Vadodara.

faq.question: What is the C-295 replacing in IAF service?
faq.answer: The C-295 is replacing the Indian Air Force's legacy fleet of Avro HS-748 transport aircraft, which have been in service since the 1960s. The 56 C-295 aircraft will provide tactical airlift capability for troop transport, paratroop drop, logistics supply, and casualty evacuation. The C-295 has a payload capacity of up to 9 tonnes and a range of up to 2,700 nautical miles (5,000 km) fully loaded.

faq.question: When will the first India-built C-295 be delivered?
faq.answer: The first fly-away C-295 was delivered from Airbus Seville in September 2023. The first India-assembled C-295 was rolled out from the TASL Vadodara FAL in October 2025. Deliveries are scheduled to continue through 2031 as the FAL ramps up to its full production rate. Exact delivery milestones for the remaining 39 India-built aircraft have not been publicly detailed.
